Press Start tuning, then bow an open string and hold it.

Reference tones

Tap a string to hear its pitch. Tap again to stop. Match it by ear, or tune against the gauge.

Tuning notes

Go A, D, G, E
Set the A first from the reference tone or a fork, then work through D, G and E. Each step leaves the earlier strings closer to where they were.
Fine tuners or pegs
Fine tuners handle moves of a few cents. Pegs do the big changes, and they should turn slowly.
Pluck, then bow
A plucked string gives a cleaner first reading. Bow it once you are close to check that the pitch holds.
Mind the room
Temperature moves pitch. Re-check after bringing the violin in from the cold. New strings keep stretching, so retune a few times.

Use offline

Install the Android app: it carries the whole toolkit and works offline from the start.

Download the Android app (APK)

Android will ask you to allow installs from your browser (Install unknown apps). Then open the downloaded file and tap Install.

If the app won’t install, add the website from Chrome instead:

  1. Open this page in Safari.
  2. Tap the Share button.
  3. Scroll down and tap Add to Home Screen.
  4. Keep Open as Web App switched on, then tap Add.
  5. Open it from the new Home Screen icon once while you have internet.
  1. Open this page in Chrome.
  2. Tap the menu button.
  3. Tap Install app, or Add to Home screen.
  4. Tap Install to confirm.
  5. Open it from the new icon once while you have internet.
  1. Open this page in Chrome or Edge.
  2. Click the install icon at the right end of the address bar.
  3. Click Install to confirm.
  4. Open it from its new icon once while you have internet.

After the first visit, it also works offline.

No install icon? Open the browser menu and choose Install Violin Toolkit. In Safari on a Mac, use File, then Add to Dock. Firefox cannot install apps, but the page still opens offline in a browser tab after one visit.

    Privacy policy

    Violin Toolkit has no accounts and no cookies. Your settings, practice time and imported tunes stay on this device. The only time the app goes online is to check for a new version (it sends the app version, the kind of app and a random number made on this device, which we count) and, on the phone builds, to fetch a built-in tune the first time you play it.
